newsitem.title: USA: NCR reports fourth quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: NCR reports fourth quarter profit.

text.p: NCR Corp., in its first earnings report since being spun off by AT&T Corp., said Tuesday it earned a fourth quarter profit compared to a big loss a year earlier and sharply narrowed its losses for the full year.
The maker of computer systems for retailers, banks and other users was spun off into a separate company by AT&T Corp. on Dec. 31.

Dayton, Ohio-based NCR suffered when it was owned by AT&T, in part because more nimble competitors beat it into faster-growing computer lines. Analysts have said AT&T never really understood NCR's business.
As part of a major restructuring, NCR said in September 1995 that it would no longer manufacture personal computers but would buy them from other makers and resell them as part of its systems.

The company said it had net income of $7 million, or 7 cents a share, for the fourth quarter, compared to a loss of $305 million, or $3.01 a share, in the 1995 quarter. Restructuring charges cut income by $27 million, or 27 cents a share, for the latest quarter.
Sales fell 10 percent to $2.04 billion from $2.27 billion, reflecting a decision to halt sales of personal computers and other machines to certain outlets.

"Traditional quarterly comparisons, which include results from businesses discontinued as part of our restructuring, tend to mask the solid operational achievements we made during the year in turning the business around," Chairman Lars Nyberg said.
"The challenge for NCR is very clear now," he added, "we must achieve growth in revenue and gross margins."
For the year, NCR had a net loss of $109 million, or $1.07 a share, compared to a loss of $2.28 billion, or $22.49 a share, in 1995. Sales fell 15 percent to $6.96 billion from $8.16 billion.
AT&T, which bought NCR for $7.5 billion in 1991, said in September, as it was preparing for the spin-off, that NCR's losses totalled about $3.9 billion since 1993.
Investors welcomed the results, and NCR stock jumped $3.25 to $38.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
The financial results were restated as if NCR had been an independent company, a spokesman said.
